lines.cap: He got so big, the government chopped him into thirty four pieces. And he got even richer.
lines.say: He got so big, the government chopped him into thirty four pieces. And he got even richer.

lines.cap: John D. Rockefeller. He started Standard Oil in 1870. Within ten years, it controlled about ninety percent of the oil refined in America.
lines.say: John D. Rockefeller. He started Standard Oil in 1870. Within ten years, it controlled about ninety percent of the oil refined in America.

lines.cap: He crushed rivals with secret deals from the railroads. Cheaper shipping for him. Higher prices for everyone else. Sell to him, or go broke.
lines.say: He crushed rivals with secret deals from the railroads. Cheaper shipping for him. Higher prices for everyone else. Sell to him, or go broke.

lines.cap: Cartoons drew his company as a giant octopus, with its arms wrapped around Congress.
lines.say: Cartoons drew his company as a giant octopus, with its arms wrapped around Congress.

lines.cap: In 1911, the Supreme Court ordered Standard Oil broken up. Into thirty four separate companies.
lines.say: In 1911, the Supreme Court ordered Standard Oil broken up. Into thirty four separate companies.

lines.cap: But Rockefeller owned shares in all thirty four. Their stock prices went up. Within about a year, his fortune roughly doubled.
lines.say: But Rockefeller owned shares in all thirty four. Their stock prices went up. Within about a year, his fortune roughly doubled.

lines.cap: Those pieces still exist. Exxon. Mobil. Chevron. Some of the biggest companies on Earth.
lines.say: Those pieces still exist. Exxon. Mobil. Chevron. Some of the biggest companies on Earth.

lines.cap: He also handed out shiny dimes to strangers. Millions of them. Good PR.
lines.say: He also handed out shiny dimes to strangers. Millions of them. Good PR.
